item.title: Gov Eno Approves 13th-Month Pension For Retirees
item.description: Akwa Ibom State Governor, Pastor Umo Eno, has approved the payment of a 13th-month pension bonus to all pensioners in the State, as well as a N10,000 one-time welfare support for November, 2026. Governor Umo Eno disclosed this during the presentation of a Merit Award by the State Council of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, who also endorsed him for re-election in 2027. Governor Eno, who was particularly impressed by their sense of gratitude and quality organisation, assured that the Government under his leadership will continue to prioritize the welfare of pensioners and elderly citizens in the State. “This is indeed humbling to me. It shows that you are truly technocrats with a laudable sense of organization. You may be retired but not tired. I celebrate and appreciate you greatly. “I am now directing that N10,000 be added to the November 2026 pension payment of every pensioner in support of your welfare,” he said. Governor of Akwa Ibom State, Pastor Umo Eno waves to retirees at the meeting. He urged them to equally enroll in the State’s health insurance scheme, which he said was free for 65-year-olds and above, to enable them to enjoy quality healthcare and a good rest across the state. Gov noted that he had promised to clear the backlog of gratuities, stressing that N100 billion has so far been paid, from the accumulated N111 billion since 2012, assuring that before the end of his first term, the balance will be cleared. He commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for making funds available to states, which, according to him, has made it possible for him to keep to his promise of clearing the arrears of gratuity. Governor Umo Eno during the presentation of a Merit Award by the State Council of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners. Earlier, in his welcome remarks, the State Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, Pastor Sylvester Nkodo, thanked the Governor for his compassionate and impactful leadership, describing his commitment to the welfare of the elderly and retired public servants as heartwarming and unprecedented. He also noted that Gov. Eno’s policies have significantly improved their living standard and lifted them from abject poverty to a life of dignity. He expressed gratitude to the Governor for the release of over N100 billion for the payment of inherited gratuities dating back to 2012 and prayed that God will grant the wishes of pensioners by granting him a second term in 2027. Following a motion moved and seconded by Comrade James Inim and Dr. Mrs. Uduak Udoaka, respectively, the pensioners unanimously endorsed President Tinubu, Senate President Godswill Akpabio, Governor Umo Eno and other candidates of the APC for re-election in 2027. The post Gov Eno Approves 13th-Month Pension For Retirees appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Who Checks on the Person Everyone Calls?
item.description: At 11:47 p.m., the family WhatsApp group suddenly comes alive. “Good evening, fam. Please, we have an emergency.” Before the second message arrives, everyone already knows who will be tagged. The eldest daughter who always knows what to do. The brother with the most stable job. The aunty abroad. The uncle in Lagos who “knows somebody.” The cousin with a car. The friend who always picks up, even at an unreasonable hour. In many Nigerian families, care has a name and a phone number. It belongs to the person who pays the unexpected bill, makes the difficult call, accompanies someone to the hospital, settles the family disagreement, or says, “Don’t worry, I’ll handle it.” We call them strong. Responsible. Dependable. We praise their shoulders without asking if they hurt. This is the human question at the heart of AXA Mansard’ s Culture of Care campaign: “ Who cares for the person everyone calls”? The Person Who Always Finds a Way Every family, friendship circle and workplace has one. Sometimes, she is the firstborn daughter who became a second mother long before she was ready. She remembers birthdays, school fees, hospital appointments, and the details everyone else forgets. Sometimes, he is the brother whose first good job quietly turned him into the family’s emergency fund and dependable source. His salary has not grown significantly, but the number of people depending on it has. Other times, it is the mom who serves everyone’s food before sitting down to eat. The father who never admits that he is worried. The friend who listens to everyone’s problems but rarely talks about her own. The colleague who carries the team whenever someone falls behind. These people are often so good at caring that we stop seeing the effort involved. We see the transfer alert, but not the personal plan they postponed. We see the paid bills, but not the hours spent calling doctors, arranging transport, and sitting beside a bed. We see the calm voice saying, “Everything will be fine,” but not the fear or uncertainty behind it. That person everyone calls may also be tired. They may worry about money, struggle with their health, or quietly wonder who would come through for them if they could no longer carry everyone else. Care Has More Than One Currency In Nigeria, many conversations about family responsibility often begin and end with money. Who paid the school fees? Who sent money home? Who handled the rent? Who covered the medical emergency? These questions matter, especially as the cost of living continues to stretch households. But money is only one currency of care. Care can also be time ! The sitting in traffic to pick up someone else’s child; the night spent at the hospital bedside; the regular reminder to an elderly parent to remember their medication. Or listening to the same worry repeatedly because the person telling you has nowhere else to take it. Care can be access ! Advice. Attention. Prayer. Food. Transport. Encouragement. A job referral. item.title: Dino Melaye throws Quranic citation challenge at Tinubu
item.description: Former Kogi West Senator, Dino Melaye, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to a Quranic citation contest following the President’s recent pilgrimage to Saudi Arabia. Melaye issued the challenge in a post on his X handle on Monday, saying he was ready to compete with Tinubu in citing verses from the Quran after his return to Nigeria. He wrote, “Now that Alhaji Bola Tinubu is in Umrah. Immediately he comes back, I challenge him to a Quranic citation competition with me. No one can mock God, SDM.” The challenge comes after Tinubu’s spiritual visit to Saudi Arabia, where he performed Umrah, the lesser Hajj, and was granted access to enter the Holy Kaaba alongside members of his delegation. In a statement on Monday by Bayo Onanuga, Special Adviser to the President on Information & Strategy, Tinubu said he prayed for wisdom and resilience to continue serving Nigerians while reaffirming his commitment to national development and prosperity. “Well, I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that prayer has been granted. Before the 2023 election, I did the same thing. I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then, and He did. And I promised that I would come back to thank Him,” the statement quoted Tinubu. Tinubu also expressed gratitude to Saudi Arabia’s King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for granting him and members of his delegation the rare privilege of praying inside the Holy Kaaba. Tinubu, reflecting on Surah Aal-Imran, Verse 26 of the Holy Quran, said all power and authority belonged to Almighty Allah, who could grant leadership to anyone and take it away at will. “There is no other God but Almighty Allah. He is the giver and the taker. He owns power and authority. He says, ‘If I give you, use it well. If you don’t use it in accordance with my dictates, I can take it from you and give it to another person. I am the only One who has that authority,” he said. He also reaffirmed his commitment to national development, declaring, “My commitment to Project Nigeria is higher. I am determined to usher in prosperity and fully develop the country, consistent with the wish of Allah and the support of the people.” On the economy, Tinubu expressed optimism about the country’s progress, saying, “The foundation is solid, and the economy has come out of the dark tunnel. This is inspiring.” He also stressed the need to invest in young Nigerians, adding, “We need to build a future for our youth. item.title: [VIDEO] God Has Granted Me Wisdom To Continue To Serve Nigerians – Tinubu
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has said that God has granted him the wisdom to continue to rule Nigerians following his recent visit to the holy mosque in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. President Tinubu, while speaking with journalists, said he felt fulfilled after observing prayers at the holy mosque in Ka’aba. “I feel fulfilled and grateful to Almighty Allah for giving us the opportunity and the health. The day went very well. “The prayer is for Allah to convert our diversity. Nigeria is full of diversity. It is made up of all the faiths. May Allah convert all the diversity to prosperity for the country. That is my prayer”. Speaking on his requests while there, Tinubu noted that God had granted him the “wisdom to continue to serve Nigerians”. “Well, I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that has been granted. “Prior to the 2023 election, I did the same thing. I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then. He did, and I promised that I would come back to thank him, Almighty Allah. “There is no other God but him. He is the giver and the taker. “He owns the power. He said, use it well. If you don’t use it in accordance with my dictates, I can take it from you and give it to another person. “So, I have faith in that and believe extremely well that he has done me a favour to be the president of this great country. On commitment to Nigeria, President Tinubu noted that his commitment is “higher” and determined to bring prosperity. “My commitment is higher, and committed to bringing prosperity. To develop the country consistently with the wish of Allah and the support of the people”. He enjoined all to serve Allah and be guided by their consciences. “It is important to put Allah first. Then follow your conscience, follow the right path that will lead Nigeria to that greatness.” He reiterated that the economy was out of the woods and that the reforms were yielding good results. “The foundation is solid. The economy has come out of the dark tunnel. It is inspiring. We need to build the future for our youths. “If we don’t invest for their future, in 50 years from now, how do we want to be remembered as leaders? I am not looking for anything else.” He thanked management of the Ka’abha for granting him access to the holy mountain, saying that it was a historical moment for him. He assured Nigerians that the current economic challenges would soon be over. “I want to thank everyone for the faith and recognition. I can’t believe that the colour of the Ka’aba was green-white-green. I thank them for the hospitality and recognition given to me as a leader of the delegation. “We are all facing challenges and hostility around us. We will overcome it with faith in the Almighty. “I am grateful forever. I thank the King and the royal crown prince. It is their honour to have allowed me to enter the Ka’aba. It is history.” The post [VIDEO] God Has Granted Me Wisdom To Continue To Serve Nigerians – Tinubu appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Tinubu inherited Nigeria on brink of collapse from Buhari — Plateau gov
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has said President Bola Ahmed Tinubu inherited a Nigerian economy that was “tottering on the brink of collapse” from the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari in 2023. Mutfwang stated this on Monday during the formal inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Campaign Council in Jos, where he also defended the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms and urged Plateau residents to support the President in the 2027 election. “Where did President Tinubu meet Nigeria in 2023? He met Nigeria, tottering on the brink of collapse, Nigeria that could not service its external debts, Nigeria that would not even allow businesses outside the country to take their proceeds back home.” “And that is why some international airlines stopped flying to Nigeria, because they could not get the dollars to take back their money.” “Our external reserve was down to just a little over $3 billion, from the over $40 billion it had accumulated for decades.” “Today, by the grace of God, we have a healthy external reserve of over $50 billion,” he said. Mutfwang further alleged that the previous administration resorted to printing money to manage the economy, claiming that more than N30 trillion was printed. “When the President took over in 2023, the government that he succeeded had run out of ideas on how to manage the economy, and they resorted to printing money in the Central Bank. “They printed over N30 trillion, which went down the drain.” “Today, by the grace of God, the Central Bank has stabilised, and that deficit has been done away with,” the governor said. On fuel subsidy, Mutfwang described the system under the previous administration as fraudulent, alleging that the country borrowed money to pay claims supported by what he called fictitious documents. “I say it was a fraud because we were borrowing money to pay people who brought fictitious documents. They never brought any wealth. They brought fictitious documents, claimed monies and subsidies. “You cannot continue to borrow money to give to thieves. You have to stop it at some point. And when it is stopped, there will be a payback; there will be a recovery time,” he said. The governor said the availability of fuel had improved despite the increase in its cost, recalling the long queues that previously characterised fuel stations across the country. “Today, by the grace of God, we have solved one side of the equation. Today fuel is available. It may not be cheap, but it is available.” “Those of us who are in my age bracket or a little below will remember the times when we spent days in petrol stations queuing for fuel that we could hardly get. But we have been able to resolve that,” Mutfwang said. Vintage fun: Prodding AI agents using retro hardware just because you can
item.description: From the department of "pointless but still cool" comes word of some kit being repurposed as a terminal for AI agents. AWS developer advocate Darko Mesaroš has connected a teletype to a modern command-line interface to revel in the delight of interacting with today's AI technology via a combination of a DECwriter and fanfold paper, or the display and keyboard of a computer whose heyday ended 40 years ago. Mesaroš' project involved AWS Kiro , a Command Line Interface (CLI) and agentic coding service. We would, however, contend that this is more about seeing what retro hardware can be made to do. Two problems needed solving: getting data to and from the teletype, and formatting the output to work on a piece of kit from another era of computing. He used Hayes modem emulation to deal with the serial connection, and Agent Client Protocol (ACP) for working with Kiro. Mesaroš used a WiModem232 for the former. The device emulates a standard Hayes-compatible modem and, according to Mesaroš, "Folks initially used this to connect Commodore 64s to BBSes in the modern era" (he started his computing journey with a Commodore 64). The latter, getting the Kiro CLI to work on a Teletype, was a little more complicated. Kiro's CLI isn't really suitable for a teleprinter capable of 30 characters per second, after all. A simple Rust application took Kiro's output (obtained via ACP) and turned it into something that a teletype, or dumb terminal, could handle. As we said, seemingly pointless, but making it work required knowledge of Rust, competence with containers, an understanding of ACP, and more than a little creative thinking. So, while one might argue it is pointless from a technical perspective, it is wonderfully educational otherwise. The repository is available and focuses on Kiro for obvious reasons (Mesaroš is an AWS developer advocate after all), but in a chat with The Register , Mesaroš said the concept was portable. He said, "Any coding assistant or any harness that supports ACP, this should work, right? I built it for Kiro, but it uses the standard ACP protocol, so I could easily plug in Claude Code or Codex. Anything that basically can serve as an ACP server should be perfectly fine. "Blessed be the standards, right?" There might be some issues. "The biggest problem with this thing is that it doesn't really handle packet drops at all," he explained. "Like, if you drop packets, they're just gone. There're no retries. It's just spitting information out." And then there is buffering. Or the lack of it. Mesaroš said, "There's actually no buffering happening here. Literally, it just comes down through the fire hose through this serial device, and the bottleneck itself is the serial device." Mesaroš had toyed with using the GPIO pins on a Raspberry Pi, but settled on the serial device instead, since everything worked "out of the box." "It's kind of cheating," he admitted, "but it's also kind of good." Mesaroš collects vintage hardware, with a stash that ranges

item.title: The best new popular-science books of November 2026
item.description: Richard Dawkins, who has a new book out this month Adam Ihse/TT/Shutterstock As seasonal storms take many of us by surprise, it’s time to head for the certainty of indoors, and a decent book (or two). We have some really intriguing titles this month, including a profoundly odd-sounding book by a forest that shares author rights with humans, and some terrifying night terrors that may teach us a lot about our brains. Oh, and if you want to stop trying to control everything around you, try surrendering to a higher power – of your choice, naturally. Radical Surrender by Anna Lembke In a complex world, the pressure to control your life is immense: from removing annoying noises around you to slavishly avoiding missing out on living your best life, to keeping your relationship, children and health on track in every way imaginable. It’s overwhelming. Surely we can’t keep it up? According to Anna Lembke’s new book, Radical Surrender: Letting go in a world addicted to change , there is a way out. The word ”addicted” in the subtitle offers a clue here: this is the author of the bestselling book Dopamine Nation , in which she looked at pleasure and pain – and the critical task of finding a delicate balance between them, especially in an age of unprecedented high-reward, high-dopamine stimuli, mostly delivered digitally. In this new book, we are promised tools to help us let go of our desire for control, but we have to follow Lembke’s advice and acknowledge a “power greater than ourselves, however we define it, and give our will over to that power: less mastery and more a return to mystery”. As an addiction medicine psychiatrist and head of Stanford University’s Addiction Medicine Dual Diagnosis Clinic in California, this “radical surrender” should be scientifically argued. Watch out for our review on 5 November. Advertisement Free newsletter Sign up to Book Club Sign up to newsletter Big Math by Steven Strogatz and Alex Townsend Let’s face it: our every move, from our next Google search to our latest Netflix selection, is utterly dependent on numbers, and AI is now an everyday reality. We have no choice but to face up to the overwhelming presence of mathematics, small, medium – or big. In Big Math: The hidden codes that run our world , Steven Strogatz and Alex Townsend (both leading mathematicians at Cornell University, New York) set out to show how relatively familiar concepts such as matrices, vectors, Markov chains, linear algebra and the like lie at the heart of computer science and quantum computing – essential for us all to know, say its publishers, if we’re to “comprehend the changes sweeping the world”. item.title: What is Starshield? A look at SpaceX's military satellite network
item.description: null SpaceX is building and operating two satellite networks at the moment, Starlink and Starshield. What’s the difference between the two, and who uses them? For more than a week in October 2026, Ukrainian drone operators found their high-speed satellite links shut off. Officials in Kyiv said that terminals for SpaceX ’s Starshield network stopped working at speeds of above 160 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour) from Oct. 14, hampering efforts to conduct defensive operations and intercept Russian drones. Full connectivity was restored on Oct. 24, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The arguments over who did what continue, but the affair highlighted how little is publicly understood about Starshield — what it is, how it relates to Starlink , and how it is operated. What is Starlink? Starlink is SpaceX’s commercial, mass-market satellite internet service. The company says it now has more than 11,000 Starlink broadband and mobile satellites in orbit, operating approximately 342 miles (550 kilometers) above Earth. This follows years of deployment using the company's Falcon 9 rocket.. The network serves consumers, enterprises and government customers across more than 160 countries. It is owned and operated by SpaceX. Anyone from a rural household to an airline can buy a terminal and a service plan. Governments are also customers, with public agencies using Starlink for a range of purposes including connectivity, disaster response and national security, notably in the case of Ukraine in the wake of the invasion by Russia , which began in February 2022 and is ongoing. What is Starshield? Starshield is SpaceX’s network for serving national security customers. The company announced the program in December 2022 , stating it would apply Starlink technology and SpaceX's launch capability to government needs, initially in three areas: Earth observation, communications and hosted payloads. "They are using the same satellite buses," says Bleddyn Bowen, associate professor of astropolitics at Durham University in the U.K. “They look the same, but they have a lot more kit on them that allows them to do more things. They provide similar broadband internet, but with more secure hardware and software and hardened systems.” The company says it has won multi-billion-dollar, multiyear contracts from the U.S. military in 2026 for Starshield-related services. Some Starshield satellites may also carry sensors for intelligence and surveillance. But much about Starshield is secretive, with its finances not revealed and launches often classified. Starshield makeup Starshield is made up of a range of different assets, including spy satellites, military data satellites, and secure communications for ground users. The spy satellites are sent into orbit in launches for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office (NRO), for a "proliferated architecture" of spy satellites , including electro-optical, radar and relay spacecraft. item.title: Oyedepo ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌‍⁠​‌⁠​‍‌​tasks Africa with indigenous solutions to challenges
item.description: The Chancellor of Covenant University, Ota, Ogun, Dr David Oyedepo, has urged African countries to look inward and deploy indigenous solutions to address the continent’s numerous challenges. Oyedepo gave the advice in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Monday in Ota. He said that developing homegrown solutions to local challenges was the way forward for Africa to reduce its heavy dependence on foreign countries. “Man is created to solve his problems wherever he is planted. Therefore, African countries should provide solutions to their challenges without constantly seeking foreign assistance,” he said. The chancellor said that Africa’s slow pace of development was not because its people were Black but largely because they were blind to their potential. ‘’Africans should take absolute responsibility for their destiny,” he said. Oyedepo attributed the continent’s inability to adequately address its challenges to what he described as a “what will happen will happen” mentality. According to him, the mindset has contributed significantly to Africa’s present situation by discouraging proactive thinking and responsibility. He said that the greatness of any nation depended on the valuable contributions of individuals and organisations within its borders. ‘’Africa will make meaningful progress only when its countries recognise the importance of indigenous solutions and take responsibility for addressing their challenges rather than relying excessively on foreign assistance,” he said. The chancellor urged African leaders and citizens to harness their local knowledge, resources and capabilities to drive sustainable development across the continent. item.title: Meet the TECNO CAMON Slim: The Android Phone Made for Cool People
item.description: Remember when Android phones were chosen purely for specs, battery life, and performance, while iPhones got to be the fashion accessories? Well, those days are over. TECNO just launched the CAMON Slim in Nigeria, and it looks like it walked straight out of a fashion editorial. With its incredibly slim design, stylish colours, and standout features, the TECNO CAMON Slim brings a whole new attitude to the Android experience. It’s not just about what your phone can do anymore; it’s about how good it looks while doing it. Here are a few reasons why this phone stands out: Your Phone Is Officially Part of Your Outfit You know how the right bag, shoes, or accessories can pull an entire outfit together? That’s exactly the energy the TECNO CAMON Slim brings. At just 6.39mm thin with a gorgeous 3D-curved design, this phone looks like it belongs in a fashion lover’s collection. It’s sleek, elegant, and definitely not the kind of device you hide in a pocket. And the colours? Jungle Green, Burgundy Red, Prism Black, and Mondrian. Whether your style is minimalist, sophisticated, or unapologetically bold, there’s a CAMON Slim that matches your aesthetic. Who said your phone couldn’t be part of the drip? Even the Back of This Phone Has Main Character Energy Most phones have a nice-looking back. The TECNO CAMON Slim decided that wasn’t enough. Its interactive AI Mood Light brings the back of the phone to life with playful lighting effects and animations that respond to activities like incoming calls, notifications, and charging. Imagine placing your phone face down on a table and watching it light up with personality. It’s fun, it’s different, and it’s exactly the kind of detail that makes someone sitting beside you ask, “Wait, what phone is that?” Your iPhone Friends Can Finally Relax There’s always that one friend who takes all the pictures on their iPhone, and everyone else has to wait for them to send the photos. Sometimes, you don’t even get those pictures until three business days later. With the CAMON Slim’s Tap to Share feature, transferring pictures, videos, and other files between the CAMON Slim and compatible iPhones becomes much easier. No more turning a simple picture transfer into a group project. And that’s the kind of convenience we love to see. The Camera Understood the Assignment A good-looking phone deserves a camera that can keep up, and the CAMON Slim isn’t playing around. Its 50MP Sony LYTIA 600 Ultra Night Camera is designed to capture detailed photographs, even when the lighting isn’t perfect. Think birthday dinners, concerts, night outings, outfit pictures, and all those random moments that somehow end up becoming your favourite memories. Whether you’re the friend who takes everyone’s pictures or the one who needs 20 shots before choosing one, this camera is ready for you. item.title: Bauchi LGA chairman dies in auto crash after APM meeting
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Chairman of Zaki Local Government Area of Bauchi State, Masud Aliyu Umar, has died in a road accident while returning from an Allied Peoples Movement (APM) stakeholders’ meeting in Bauchi. Umar reportedly died on Sunday night when his private car crashed at Konkiyal Village in Darazo Local Government Area, about 100 kilometres from Bauchi metropolis. The late chairman was returning to Zaki after attending the political meeting when the accident occurred. Before his election as Zaki LGA chairman on August 17, 2026, Umar served as Director-General of the Bauchi State Emergency Management Agency, SEMA. Reacting to his death, Governor Bala Mohammed expressed shock, describing the deceased as a dedicated public servant, committed grassroots politician and compassionate leader whose contributions to public service and community development would remain indelible in the history of the state. In a condolence message issued by his media aide, Mukhtar Gidado, the governor said Umar’s tenure at SEMA was marked by his commitment to alleviating the suffering of vulnerable citizens and providing timely interventions to communities affected by emergencies and humanitarian challenges. Mohammed added that as chairman of Zaki Local Government, the deceased demonstrated commitment to grassroots development through initiatives aimed at empowering youths and women, improving livelihoods and promoting inclusive development. He described the death as a devastating loss to the deceased’s family, the people of Zaki and Bauchi State, particularly the public service and local government administration. The governor urged the family, political associates, friends and people of Zaki Local Government to find strength and comfort in Almighty Allah during the difficult period. The funeral prayer is scheduled for Monday, November 2, 2026, at 2pm at the Palace of the District Head, Mur Mur, Zaki Local Government Area of Bauchi State. item.title: Transfer Centre LIVE! 'Balde could leave Barcelona with Man Utd interested'
Microsoft's moolah mountain is more massive than ever. It just doesn't want the people who built it
item.description: Capitalism can seem so perverse. Take Microsoft, which is celebrating record financial performance by inviting 60,000 employees to consider continuing their careers outside the company . Voluntary redundancy may seem to make sense when a company's running out of cash, but Microsoft is dripping with the stuff . It was a very good fiscal '26 at Redmond. Its Azure business is up over 40 percent, it's has 30 million paid seats on CoPilot, revenues are through the roof, and it has so much moolah it returned $10.2 billion to shareholders in the form of dividends and share repurchases. This latter move probably soothed CEO Satya Nadella, who suffered, due to the vagaries of C-suite reimbursement and incentive packages, a 6 percent cut in his pocket money . But as he’s also a stockholder with about 0.01 percent of the company, his share of the cash return presumably eased the pain. He won't have been offered redundo. Jenkins, the large wheelbarrow if you please. Microsoft, then, can afford all its employees, each who contributes about $1.5 million to SatNad's bottom line. The "massive efficiencies and ROI of AI" make a great line for a company flogging magic LLM juice, but the evidence remains elusive. AI is, of course, still the reason. Nothing else matters these days. It’s just that it's not today's AI. Among all the fulsome figures, analysts noted that Microsoft's capital expenditure wasn't as spendy as expected. Quite a lot has been pushed into next calendar year, not because it's not there to be spent – Microsoft could build a 1:1 scale model of the Vatican filled with robot priests if it wanted – but because so much it wanted to mash the Buy Now button for was "Out of stock. More expected soon." This is bad. MS added 88 datacenters in its most recent full financial year. That’s not enough datacenters for a cloud business expected to grow by half again in 2027, and hugely not enough to do the other thing. Lags in the cadence of deforestation, dewatering and detonation of the planet can't be tolerated. Thus there are contracts signed to get things back on track PDQ, with mucho, mucho, mucho sponduiks. Microsoft is hinting, those selfsame analysts say, that it will have to go to the debt market and go into " negative free cash flow " territory in 2028. In other words, as well as spending its own bank, the company will be taking out massive loans. This is why Billy and Bhavya Dev have to go. The cost of borrowing depends on the financial health of the borrower, and that boils down to how much profit you're making from the money you earn. A big round of redundancies, which are very costly in themselves, sits on the books of the year they happen. The hole in expenditure left by the vanished salaries lives on. The capital must flow. Will this work? Last week, we listed the reasons why it might not — price competition between rivals and increasingly powerful local and open weight models, supply side shortages, you know the litany by now. item.title: [Updated] Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if US agrees to demands
item.description: Iran on Monday said it was ready to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US agrees to its conditions, having previously proposed a one-week timeline. “The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran’s good-faith approach,” said foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei. “We have stated that, if Iran’s demands are met, it would be possible to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz and resume the negotiating process within a short period.” He said an exchange of messages was ongoing with the United States via mediators and that “everything depends” on the US side accepting the Iranian demands. “Only then can we discuss the subsequent stages.” Since the Middle East war broke out in late February, Iran has claimed control over Hormuz, a vital energy conduit for shipping. It regularly targets vessels that attempt to cross the strait without its authorisation, while the US has in retaliation imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports. In September, Iran initially proposed a seven-day plan that it conveyed to the US through Qatar, which would have seen Tehran reopen Hormuz on the sixth day after the US met Iranian demands. Those demands include ending the Middle East war on all fronts, the unfreezing of Iranian assets abroad, lifting sanctions on its oil sector, and an end to the US naval blockade. In an interview with Al Jazeera released on Sunday, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Washington must accept a new route agreed between Iran and Oman for transit through the strait. He said the US must also remove sanctions imposed in recent months and reduce American troop numbers in the region. Washington has since August rolled out a fresh raft of sanctions, part of what it called “economic asphyxiation” of Iran. The United States and Israel have in recent days also intensified threats to renew attacks on Iran amid crucial elections in both countries. On Saturday, US President Donald Trump said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets including Pickaxe mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility. “Any act of aggression against Iran, any military attack against Iran, by whatever means, will be met with a powerful, immediate and comprehensive response from us,” said Baqaei during a foreign ministry briefing Monday. The post [Updated] Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if US agrees to demands appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: In California, illegal border crossings plummet under Trump administration

item.title: Meet Mo Odukoya: Pastor Jimmy Introduces His Wife as The Fountain of Life Church’s New First Lady
item.description: Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and Pastor Mo Odukoya pose together following their formal church introduction. If you’re a member of The Fountain of Life Church and you were at yesterday’s service, we’re a little jealous. What do you mean you got to witness Pastor Jimmy Odukoya introduce his wife, Mo Jasmine Daniel , to the congregation in person? Yes, right there at the church’s headquarters in Ilupeju, Lagos, the senior pastor had a special person to introduce, and he made sure everyone knew exactly who she was. As she joined him at the altar, he introduced her as Pastor Mo Odukoya , the church’s new first lady, and the congregation welcomed the couple with cheers and applause. Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and his wife, Mo Jasmine Daniel, holding hands during their official introduction at The Fountain of Life Church. But before that introduction, Pastor Jimmy had a little story to tell. He spoke about how he had been navigating life alone since becoming the church’s senior pastor, and how he had been searching for someone to share the journey with. Well, it looks like that search has come to an end. He invited Mo to join him, and the two walked up to the altar together, marking the moment with a warm reception from the congregation. Pastor Jimmy Odukoya introduces his wife, Mo Jasmine Daniel, on stage at The Fountain of Life Church in Ilupeju, Lagos. For those who know Pastor Jimmy beyond the pulpit, there’s quite a bit to his story. He took over as senior pastor of The Fountain of Life Church in 2023, following the passing of his father, the late Pastor Taiwo Odukoya , who co-founded the ministry with his wife, Pastor Bimbo Odukoya . He is also an actor and musician, and film audiences may recognise him as Oba Ade in the 2022 historical film The Woman King , where he starred alongside Viola Davis . Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and Mo Jasmine Daniel after announcing their marriage to the congregation. And now, there’s a new chapter to this story with Mo. Introduced to the congregation as Pastor Mo Odukoya, she is the daughter of Reverend Theophilus and Bolaji Daniel . She also took a moment to address the church, expressing her pleasure and honour at joining the ministry family. The couple also made sure their outfits were in sync for the occasion. Pastor Jimmy wore a structured burnt-orange native outfit with dark detailing on the cuffs and a matching necklace, while Pastor Mo chose a long-sleeved, floor-length dress in orange and copper patterns, finished with a matching clutch and accessories. Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and his new wife, Mo Jasmine Daniel, following their church introduction at The Fountain of Life Church. *** Photo Credit: Pastor Jimmy Odukoya/Instagram The post Meet Mo Odukoya: Pastor Jimmy Introduces His Wife as The Fountain of Life Church’s New First Lady appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: Britain's driverless dream hits a roundabout of awkward questions
item.description: As robotaxis continue trials in London, an independent research group thinks the UK needs to answer some serious questions before heading any further down the road. To kick off, the sovereignty question, or "Will Britain become dependent on autonomous vehicle services for any key activities and what fallback options will exist if a supplier fails or withdraws?" as the Institute for Driverless Transport (IfDT) puts it. Another question concerns employment: "To what extent does professional driving form part of the UK's employment safety net and how will this function be recreated if demand for professional drivers is significantly reduced?" The objective for IfDT — an independent UK research and convening body focused on the consequences of autonomous vehicles — is to cast the net a bit wider than simply thinking about whether the software is sufficient to navigate London’s wiggly streets and narrow alleys. The research draws on work with operators trying to bring AVs to London and the regulators responsible for policy. It also relied on more than 30 conversations with councils, operators, industry, unions, charities, insurers, lawyers and universities. James Hutt, IfDT co-founder, said: "What struck us most in the interviews was how far this reaches: into jobs, public services, the built environment and national resilience. The people who know those areas best are rarely part of the conversation about AVs. "Our next step is to bring funding and researchers together with the businesses and public bodies that need answers. If you can fund research or offer a place to test it, we would like to hear from you." In August, Transport for London (TfL) granted private hire licences to autonomous vehicle operators provided that a human driver is present during journeys. Wayve and Uber have since launched self-driving rides in the UK capital, with 15 electric Ford Mustangs, equipped with the Wayve AI driver, set to pick up passengers with a safety driver on board. UK company Wayve also demoed a Nissan LEAF , running the Wayve AI Driver using NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion with self-driving equipment built more closely into the car's design. IfDT points out that Waymo and Baidu are also preparing services for London, while Uber, Pony.ai and Verne have begun testing in Manchester. The research organization said UK authorities still need to answer a long list of questions in order to shape long-term infrastructure plans for local areas and prepare for AI's impact on the labor market. The question of who needs to do this also remains unanswered, as the IfDT asks: "Which are the key public bodies that should already be anticipating the impact of AVs on their own work and who within those organisations should lead a response?"®

item.title: Entering Holy Kaaba with Tinubu a blessing beyond measure – Abdul Samad Rabiu
item.description: Billionaire industrialist and Chairman of BUA Group, Abdul Samad Rabiu, has described his entry into the Holy Kaaba alongside President Bola Tinubu as a rare spiritual privilege and an experience he would cherish for the rest of his life. Rabiu disclosed this in a Facebook post on Sunday night, sharing a photograph of himself with Tinubu He wrote, “Some moments in life are beyond words, moments that touch the soul and remain forever engraved in the heart. “Alhamdulillah, today I was profoundly humbled and blessed to be among those granted the extraordinary honour of entering the Holy Kaaba alongside His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR. “It was a once-in-a-lifetime blessing, an honour beyond measure, and a moment of divine grace that will remain etched in my heart for as long as I live.” Rabiu said his prayers at the sacred site extended beyond himself and his family to Nigeria, expressing hope for lasting peace, unity and prosperity in the country. He added, “In that most sacred of places, my thoughts and prayers were not only for myself and my family, but for our entire nation. “May Almighty Allah accept our prayers and bless our beloved nation with lasting peace, unity, and prosperity.” Rabiu was among the delegation that accompanied Tinubu to Makkah for Umrah, the lesser pilgrimage, on Friday, which included Oando Group Chief Executive Officer, Wale Tinubu, state governors and other senior government officials. Speaking at a dinner hosted for members of the delegation in Makkah on Saturday, Rabiu pledged the continued support of the business community for the administration and thanked the president for the rare spiritual opportunity. Tinubu had also told journalists after performing the Umrah that he felt fulfilled, describing the experience as spiritual. The post Entering Holy Kaaba with Tinubu a blessing beyond measure – Abdul Samad Rabiu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: RSF publishes list of press freedom 'predators': 'Dictators want to silence journalists'
item.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Thibaut Bruttin, Director General and Secretary-General of Reporters Without Borders (RSF), who says, “When a journalist is killed, it is everyone's right to know what is being endangered.” His warning captures the central democratic dilemma explored in this interview marking the United Nations' International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists. As journalists confront lethal violence, imprisonment, political intimidation and increasingly hostile working environments, the struggle for press freedom has become inseparable from a more fundamental question: who controls the public's access to truth? For RSF, press freedom is not simply a journalist's right to speak, but society's right to know.

item.title: African players in Europe: Defender Hakimi’s historic hat-trick
item.description: Reigning African Footballer of the Year and Paris Saint-Germain defender Achraf Hakimi claimed a first career hat-trick at the weekend in a 5-1 Ligue 1 rout of bottom club Le Havre. Meanwhile, Nicolas Jackson continued to defy critics from a difficult spell at Chelsea by scoring his eighth goal in 12 appearances for Aston Villa, who drew 1-1 with Fulham. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: FRANCE ACHRAF HAKIMI (Paris Saint-Germain) Morocco captain Hakimi was involved in all five goals as defending European champions and Ligue 1 leaders PSG inflicted a seventh defeat in nine matches on Le Havre. Apart from his hat-trick, he set up goals for Mika Godts and Senny Mayulu. ENGLAND NICOLAS JACKSON (Aston Villa) In-form Jackson scored again, but it was not enough for Unai Emery’s men to defeat struggling Fulham. The Senegal international coolly slotted home from Johan Manzambi’s pass for a fifth Premier League goal in his last five games. TAIWO AWONIYI (Coventry City) Awoniyi netted his first league goal for Coventry in a 3-1 win over Sunderland that hauled the Sky Blues out of the relegation zone. The Nigerian made the most of his first start since September as he won possession himself before surging into the Sunderland box and firing into the bottom corner. SPAIN YAN DIOMANDE (Real Madrid) Ivory Coast teenager Diomande completed the scoring before half-time as Real Madrid triumphed 3-0 at Racing Santander in La Liga. The record signing by the 15-time European champions lashed home from the edge of the box after 37 minutes. ITALY M’BALA NZOLA (Cagliari) Angolan Nzola gave mid-table Cagliari the lead midway through the first half, but Serie A pacesetters Lazio hit back to win 2-1 in Rome. Nzola struck from the edge of the six-yard box to net in successive matches for the first time in 70 months. GERMANY SERHOU GUIRASSY (Borussia Dortmund) His second-half goal put Borussia on track for an impressive 2-2 Bundesliga draw at leaders Bayern Munich. After Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane missed a penalty, Dortmund went to the other end of the pitch and Guirassy equalised. It brought the goal tally of the Guinea striker in all competitions to eight this season. IBRAHIM MAZA (Bayer Leverkusen) Leverkusen were outplayed by Stuttgart in a 4-2 defeat, but Maza left the pitch with his head held high. After the Algeria midfielder showcased his stunning dribbling, he scored after 79 minutes with an unstoppable header. BILAL EL KHANNOUSS (Stuttgart) El Khannouss provided the creative spark as Stuttgart snapped a run of poor form to win at Leverkusen. The Moroccan scored with a superb low shot early in the second half and helped create Stuttgart’s fourth for Ermedin Demirovic. The post African players in Europe: Defender Hakimi’s historic hat-trick appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu reaffirms commitment to Project Nigeria
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has reaffirmed his commitment to Project Nigeria, pledging to build a prosperous nation, invest in youths and pursue development guided by Almighty Allah and Nigerians’ aspirations. The president stated this on Monday while reflecting on his spiritual journey to Saudi Arabia for the lesser Hajj, during which he was granted the rare privilege of praying inside the Holy Ka’abah. King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, granted the President and members of his delegation access to the sacred structure in Makkah. At the Ka’abah, Tinubu offered prayers of gratitude to Almighty Allah for the privilege of serving as Nigeria’s president and commander-in-chief of the armed forces. Sheikh Dahlulah Muthawal of Masjid al-Haram led the President into the Ka’abah. Tinubu thanked King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for granting him and members of his delegation the opportunity to enter the Holy Ka’abah and offer prayers. He described the honour as historic and a deeply cherished spiritual experience, reflecting the longstanding bonds of friendship, mutual respect and cooperation between Nigeria and Saudi Arabia. “I want to say a big thank you for the faith, for the recognition. I can’t believe the fencing of the Ka’abah is in green-white-green, which reminds us of the Nigerian identity. “I thank the Crown Prince and all the administrators of the Holy Land. I thank them for the hospitality and recognition given to me as the leader of the delegation and the country. “We are all facing challenges and hostility around us. We will overcome them with faith in God Almighty. I’m grateful forever. I thank the King and the royal Crown Prince. “It is an honour that I enjoyed, and it is gracious of them to have allowed me to enter inside the Ka’abah. This is history,” he said. The president said he prayed for wisdom and resilience to continue serving Nigerians, expressing confidence that Almighty Allah had granted his request. “Well, I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that prayer has been granted. Before the 2023 election, I did the same thing. “I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then, and He did. And I promised that I would come back to thank Him,” the President said. Reflecting on Surah Aal-Imran, Verse 26 of the Holy Qur’an, the President said sovereignty belonged ultimately to Almighty Allah, who grants and withdraws power. He said the message underscored the need for leaders to exercise authority responsibly, with humility and in the service of the people. “There is no other God but Almighty Allah. He is the giver and the taker. He owns power and authority. “He says, ‘If I give you, use it well. If you don’t use it in accordance with my dictates, I can take it from you and give it to another person. item.title: From Expertise to Intelligence: NISCO Deploys World's First Swarm-Intelligence Steel Model at Scale
item.description: Nanjing Iron & Steel Co., Ltd. (NISCO) has worked with Huawei and ecosystem partners to commercially deploy the world's first steel model powered by swarm intelligence - the YuanYe Steel Large Model (YuanYe) - across multiple scenarios at scale. This helps NISCO transition its core operations from relying on experience to being powered by data and intelligence collaboration. As a traditional manufacturer navigating the challenges of transformation and cost efficiency, NISCO has built a robust digital and intelligent foundation by adopting industry-leading products including Ascend, Kunpeng, Huawei Cloud Stack, and Pangu models. By embedding AI into every core stage of production - ironmaking, steelmaking, rolling, and quality inspection - NISCO is forging green and high-end AI-powered super steel plants. Unlike general-purpose monolithic models, YuanYe innovatively fuses multiple AI models with the steel industry's metallurgical mechanism models to create a dual-drive, multi-model cluster architecture. This architecture features a "right brain" for probabilistic computing and a "left brain" for precise and scientific decision-making. Powered by massive amounts of sensing data aggregated from millions of operational technology (OT) data points across 26 business domains, NISCO has achieved real-time digital twin mapping within its intelligent operations center, laying solid data and scenario foundations for YuanYe. This enables the entire steelmaking process to become not only visible, but also capable of precise control and intelligent assessment. Now 100 percent of NISCO's key equipment is connected and digitally controlled and its new product R&D cycles have been shortened by 50 percent, reducing annual costs by over CNY100m (approx. US$15m). As the model continues to iterate, NISCO had launched 25 business agents by October 2026. These agents cover a wide range of scenarios, from visual quality inspection and process optimization to production scheduling and operations management, setting a new benchmark for digital and intelligent steel transformation. Breakthroughs in four core scenarios: YuanYe redefines traditional operations for significant safety, efficiency, and quality gains In the ironmaking stage, AI makes traditionally invisible blast furnaces transparent. YuanYe leverages blast furnaces' internal sensor data and metallurgical mechanism analysis to perform real-time dynamic simulations of the ironmaking process. Assisted by furnace temperature prediction and health diagnosis models, furnace operators can predict temperatures and identify issues two hours in advance, with over 90 percent accuracy. This shifts furnace operations from reactive post-event remediation to proactive pre-control, increasing prime-grade molten iron yield by over 10 percent while significantly cutting unit energy consumption. item.title: Sultan Turbans two sons, Murtala Dan’Iyan as Dallatun Sokoto
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — The Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, has conferred traditional titles on two of his sons, Alhaji Murtala Abdulkadir Dan’Iyan Jarman Sokoto and 10 other distinguished Nigerians in recognition of their contributions to humanity and community development. The ceremony, held on Sunday at the Sultan’s Palace in Sokoto, also witnessed the turbaning of two biological sons of the Sultan. Alhaji Abubakar Sadiq was turbaned Sarkin Dawakin Tsakar Gida, while Alhaji Shehu Abubakar received the title of Fagacin Sokoto. The event marked the climax of a three-day programme organised by friends, associates and well-wishers of the new Dallatun Sokoto to celebrate his elevation into the traditional institution of the Sokoto Caliphate. It attracted traditional rulers, politicians, senior government officials, Islamic scholars, business executives and community leaders from within and outside Nigeria. Among those honoured were Alhaji Abubakar Hussain, who received the title of Sarkin Bai; Alhaji Aminu Isa-Buhari, Danmalikin Sokoto; Professor Mansur Ibrahim, Danmasanin Sokoto; and Professor Ishaq Oloyede, Kuliyan Sokoto. Others were Dr Peter Igoh, Kakakin Daular Usmaniya; Representative Almustapha Rabah, Bauran Sokoto; Dr Balarabe Kakale, Wakilin Makarantar Daular Usmaniya; Alhaji Bello Abbas, Wakilin Tarihin Daular Usmaniya; and Alhaji Gandi Umar, Sarkin Galmar Sarkin Musulmi. Speaking at the ceremony, the Sultan described the turbaning as a historic occasion organised by the Sultanate Council to recognise individuals whose contributions and achievements in their respective fields had distinguished them as worthy ambassadors of the Caliphate. He said the traditional institution would continue to recognise and honour sons and daughters of the Caliphate who demonstrated commitment, integrity and outstanding performance in their various endeavours. The monarch, however, reminded the new title holders that their elevation should not be regarded merely as a ceremonial honour but as a call to greater service and responsibility to their communities and society. He urged them to remain their brothers’ keepers, promote peace, unity and peaceful coexistence, and offer constructive ideas to strengthen harmonious relationships within the Caliphate, Sokoto State and Nigeria. In separate interviews after the ceremony, prominent personalities described the new Dallatun Sokoto as humble, honest and trustworthy, citing his philanthropic activities and readiness to assist people across religious, ethnic and social divides. A father figure and mentor to the new title holder, Alhaji Umarun Kwabo AA Jarman Sokoto, described him as loyal, humble and dependable, saying his commitment to the service of God and humanity had earned him the confidence of those around him. “I am optimistic that Dallatun Sokoto, Alhaji Murtala Abdulkadir Dan’Iyan Jarman Sokoto, will wear the shoes and crown in the service of God and humanity,” Kwabo said.

item.title: Iran Warns New War Could Last Longer After Trump Threatens Strikes
item.description: Iran warned on Sunday that any renewed war with the United States could last longer than the previous round of fighting, after President Donald Trump said he still had to “take care” of more targets. Diplomatic efforts to end the Middle East war have been punctuated by repeated threats from the United States and Israel to resume bombardments as they hold crucial elections. “A potential future war could last longer than previous conflict, and the American president would not be in a position to dictate the timing or the conditions of its conclusion,” said army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia, according to Iranian state television. In the most intense phase of the war, which began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, Tehran retaliated with missile and drone attacks across the region. Iran-aligned armed groups joined the fighting in Lebanon and Yemen. Akraminia’s remarks followed Trump’s suggestion that the United States could swiftly strike its remaining targets in Iran. “We still have to take care of, I would say one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes,” Trump told reporters. “You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, and you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly,” he added, referring to a suspected underground nuclear complex. Trump reiterated his threat on Sunday, telling a campaign rally in Iowa ahead of midterm elections, that he may have to give Tehran “the hammer” at some unspecified time. The warning came after US media reported that Trump had held a call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday over whether and when to ramp up combat operations against the Islamic republic. Axios quoted one US and one Israeli official saying the two leaders discussed the state of negotiations with Iran, with Netanyahu pressing the president to strike the country immediately after Tuesday’s US midterm elections and Trump eager to let negotiations play out. The Israeli source described the call as “tough”, while the US source said it was “direct”, according to Axios. Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Trump confirmed he had discussed Iran with Netanyahu, but would not elaborate. A woman walks past a mural bearing the Iranian national flag in Tehran on October 26, 2026. ‘No Geographical Limitations’ Top military and political officials in Iran have warned against any new attack. Revolutionary Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebbi on Sunday echoed a warning issued a day earlier in a written message by Iran’s new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei. “In a conflict with America, there are no geographical limitations; a vast theatre has been defined for inflicting damage upon the enemy,” Mohebbi said, according to state television. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said: “We hope the other side will exercise rationality and choose diplomacy,” adding that Iran “remains prepared for both defence and diplomacy”, according to the official IRNA news agency. item.title: Manager threatened to fire a colleague, then gave them a critical task – which they flubbed
item.description: Welcome to Monday morning, an occasion The Register marks with a new instalment of " Who, Me? " It's our reader-contributed column in which you confess to workplace mistakes and share your escapes from subsequent scrapes. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Gordon" who told us he once worked as an engineer at a major semiconductor corporation. Gordon rose to become manager of an engineering team which worked on a very popular PC chipset. One of the chaps on this team wasn't pulling his weight, so Gordon got the job of telling him to improve, or leave. "In all fairness, he was a nice guy but not a great engineer and needed to be better," Gordon told The Register. Not long after that moment of managerial unpleasantness, Gordon's team got the job of doing a full backup of the chipset's "production stepping" – the silicon equivalent of a minor point release. The idea was to create a detailed record that could be used as a restore point. "This was not a nightly backup, but a purposeful backup to retain a snapshot of the entire cleaned-up design database for future cases where we might need to spin another stepping quickly," Gordon explained. Gordon told his underperforming colleague to do the backup. "Because I was overworked, I did not think this through," he told The Register . The at-risk worker quickly proved why he was under the pump by deciding the backup wasn't necessary until the team completed the next stepping – but didn't tell anyone about that plan. Before that next stepping was done, the employee's past indiscretions caught up with him and he was let go. The story now fast-forwards six years, to a moment when Gordon learned that a customer wanted to buy the old chipset design so they could make a radiation-hardened version to use on satellites. The major semiconductor company liked the sound of that, and asked Gordon to find the backup. "My colleague and I then pieced together what had happened," he wrote. "Being good engineers, we said nothing. We searched through old nightly backup tapes until we found bits and pieces of different steppings of the design database and copied them all to one place, then handed this off to the customer." To this day, Gordon doesn't know if the customer was able to produce a useful chip from the bits of backup he cobbled together. "Did they realize they received bits and pieces of two slightly different databases? Did they care? Was the project canceled before anyone realized it?" "From then on, I was more careful about who I assigned the task of creating restore backups for each design project," he told The Register . "And I kept a record of the emails requesting backups and confirmation that backups had been done." Have you given a job to the wrong person? Or given clients slightly dodgy data? In either case, click here to send email to Who, Me? We would love to tell your tale on a future Monday. ®

item.title: You Should Treat Yourself to a Memorable Destination Birthday in 2027 If You Were Born Between 1977 and 1987
item.description: Christmas is now around the corner, and many of us will already be discussing plans for 2027. Some people will be thinking about new jobs, planning weddings or promising themselves they will finally start exercising next year. Then there are the 1977 and 1987 babies for whom 2027 won’t simply be another year. It is the year they turn fifty or forty, a major milestone in the journey of life that gets everyone asking: “So, what are we doing?” As someone born in 1988, I may not be under pressure to make a similar decision for 2027, but I am close enough to know that my turn is approaching very quickly. And truth be told, the closer I get to forty, the less interested I become in throwing a large party simply because that is what people expect. But after years of travelling, I have also realised that some of the most memorable celebrations are not necessarily the biggest. They are the ones connected to experiences. Like having a private villa breakfast which everyone will always talk about. The boat trip that almost ended with somebody losing their phone in the ocean. The birthday dinner beneath the stars. The destination everyone initially complained was too far, then refused to leave when the trip ended. That is what makes a destination party special. It does not give you one evening. It gives you several days of memories. So, if I were born in 1977 or 1987 and planning a milestone birthday for 2027, I would spend my birthday seeing the world, and these are the destination celebrations I would surely consider, even better if you’re celebrating with your friends: Bali, Indonesia You know that friendship group that has been saying, “Girls’ trip soon,” for the past five years? Every January, somebody opens the conversation again. Everyone agrees. Dates are suggested, then work happens, children happen, school fees happen, someone suddenly has a wedding; something always comes up and halts every plan. Before you know it, another year has passed. A fortieth or fiftieth birthday may finally be the excuse everyone needs, and Bali works beautifully because you can create a luxurious group experience without forcing everyone into separate hotel rooms. Imagine ten friends sharing a private villa with a swimming pool and staff. Begin with a welcome dinner. Add a spa morning, beach club, waterfalls, rice terraces and, on the birthday itself, a private chef and dinner beneath the stars. The greatest advantage of Bali is that luxury can still feel attainable. Just remember that Bali is not the place to invite people who cannot sit still. Some days, the entire plan may simply be breakfast, massage, swimming and sunset. And that is the itinerary . Private villa, poolside dinner, spa morning and sunset beach club–the perfect birthday idea. Thailand Thailand is for the celebrant who wants everything: City energy, beautiful beaches, nightlife, shopping, culture and food. It gives you enough value for money to stop your guests from sending angry voice notes about the

item.title: 'The Sea God Surveys': Watch Rocket Lab launch Japanese Earth-observing satellite today
item.description: null Rocket Lab will launch its 99th mission to date today (Nov. 2), and you can watch the action live. An Electron rocket is scheduled to lift off from Rocket Lab's New Zealand site today, during a window that opens at 11:30 a.m. EST (1630 GMT; 5:30 a.m. on Nov. 3 local New Zealand time), The mission, which Rocket Lab calls "The Sea God Surveys," will carry an Earth-observing radar satellite for the Japanese company iQPS. You can watch it live via Rocket Lab starting about 30 minutes before launch, and Space.com will carry the company's feed if, as expected, it's made available. The patch for Rocket Lab's "The Sea God Surveys" mission, which is expected to launch on Nov. 2, 2025. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) "The Sea God Surveys" will be Rocket Lab's 10th launch to date for iQPS, which is assembling a constellation of three dozen synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO). SAR satellites offer advantages over those that view our planet in optical wavelengths. They can peer through cloud cover, for example, and study our planet at night as well as during the day. Today's launch will be the 99th overall for Rocket Lab and the 90th for the two-stage, 59-foot-tall (18 meters) Electron, which gives small satellites dedicated rides to space. The workhorse vehicle has already flown 16 times this year. Rocket Lab's other nine launches to date have been conducted by HASTE , a suborbital version of Electron that allows customers to test their tech in the hypersonic flight environment. HASTE (short for "Hypersonic Accelerator Suborbital Test Electron") debuted in June 2023 and generally flies classified payloads.

item.title: Chap who coded Google’s Pac-Man clone reveals how the game freaked out Firefox
item.description: A designer named Marcin Wichary has revealed the story of how he freaked out a decent slab of the world’s Firefox-using population with Pac-Man. Wichary has held senior design roles at Figma, Medium, and Google. As he wrote here , in 2010 Google decided to celebrate the 30 th anniversary of Pac-Man by changing its logo at Google.com to a playable version of the game. The Google of 2010 could still mention its motto of the time, “Don’t be evil,” without making anyone who heard it guffaw incredulously. The company’s frequent changes to the logo on its homepage – called Google Doodles , and which persist to this day – were still a notable part of net culture. Wichary got the job of building the playable logo, and tweaking Pac-Man to replace its usual maze with a course that instead navigated around the letters GOOGLE. “It was, frankly, a terrifying proposition,” Wichary wrote. “The homepage was then a very important destination, and my job title was only adjacent to ‘software engineer.’ But I started researching the game and recreating it all in HTML and CSS." Google wanted a full Pac-Man experience, including sound, "because so many of Pac-Man’s sounds are beyond iconic: the starting melody, the waka-wakas, the death jingle." Wichary began work before Google sought permission from Pac-Man’s owner Namco, because the search giant was “planning to wow them with a close-to-finished doodle.” “The project was … going really well. I had fun coding the game and we seemed to have fun playing it. Namco eventually got onboard, too,” he wrote. Google liked the game work so much, higher-ups decided it would be a great idea to have it start automatically if visitors to google.com stayed idle for ten seconds. The designer liked that idea. “If there was anything scary about it at the time, it was only the thought of my code getting even more exposure – but I wasn’t worried about distraction, since the homepage was not a destination page you would ever linger on.” What Google didn’t realise was that some people lingered on the home page without ever knowing they were there. Those people used the Firefox browser with an extension called CoolPreviews that let users hover over a link to see a preview of a web page. “The extension would quietly start at the same time Firefox was opened,” Wichary explained. “And it would immediately, in the background, invisibly and unbeknownst to the user, open a website.” That website was Google’s home page, which now featured an auto-playing and version of Pac-Man that CoolPreviews users simply did not expect. Which explained why, not long after setting the Pac-Man doodle live, Google received plenty of praise, but also reports about computers making strange noises due to CoolPreviews invisibly opening the noisy game. “I pushed a patch within hours,” Wichary wrote, explaining that he added a mute button and a requirement to click something to make the game and its noises start. item.title: APOD: 2026 November 2 – A Long Cloud on Mars
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 2 – A… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. A Long Cloud on Mars Explanation: What’s causing this unusually long cloud on Mars ? Known as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC) and first recorded by NASA’s Viking Orbiter 2 in 1977, the strange cloud has been imaged in greater detail more recently by ESA ’s robotic Mars Express spacecraft. The featured image is from 2018. The cloud forms only during spring and summer seasons and then only during morning hours. Made of water-ice, the most familiar process that causes cloud crystals to form around bits of dust would fail due to the thinness and lack of dust high in the Martian atmosphere . Leading speculation holds that dust is not involved. After the cloud forms near the volcano Arsia Mons , wind blows the cloud downstream — creating a tail that can extend over 1500 kilometers. Efforts to better understand AMEC s will continue, an understanding that may bolster a more complete view of cloud formation on Earth . item.title: Pennsylvania’s Grand Canyon
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Pennsylvania’s Grand Canyon Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search October 25, 2026 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison North-central Pennsylvania is canyon country with an Appalachian flair. Pine Creek Gorge reaches depths of about 1,500 feet (460 meters) along its gently curving path through the forests of the Allegheny Plateau . Instead of the steep rock walls characteristic of canyons in the desert Southwest, lushly vegetated slopes outline the dramatic topography. In autumn, greens give way to a palette of reds and golds sought out by leaf peepers. Nicknamed the “Grand Canyon of Pennsylvania,” the gorge runs for some 45 miles (72 kilometers) from Ansonia south to Pine Creek’s confluence with the West Branch Susquehanna River, reaching its greatest depths around Waterville. The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on the NASA-USGS Landsat 8 satellite captured this image of Pine Creek Gorge on October 25, 2026, when colorful fall foliage was on display. Glaciers played a key role in the canyon’s formation, though ice itself did not carve it. Pine Creek once flowed to the north , opposite of what it does today. As glaciers advanced into the region from the northeast during the last ice age, they dammed the river and filled the valley with lakes. Those lakes eventually overflowed, sending water streaming to the south. Autumn colors emerge along Pine Creek Gorge in this view from Colton Point State Park on October 11, 2009. fishhawk , via Flickr When the ice receded, Pine Creek was already becoming entrenched in its southward course. Rocks and sand left behind by the melting ice further prevented the water from turning back north. Glacial meltwater continued to rush through the valley, deepening and shaping it into its current form. Today, the hillsides around the gorge are blanketed in northern hardwood and mixed oak forest, sprinkled with hemlock and white pine. In autumn, the deciduous trees impart red and gold hues to the landscape akin to the rock of the famous Arizona canyon . item.title: India floats AI plan under which ‘The model travels to the data, rather than the data travelling to the model’
item.description: As debate and legal argument continue over the extent to which developers of large language models are entitled to feed the world’s data into their systems without paying for it, India’s government has come up with an idea to regulate and secure the flow of information. India’s motive is to create AI models trained on local data, because it thinks offshore model-makers won’t be motivated to address the nation’s issues or to ensure owners of data stay in control. The scheme India’s Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) thinks can make that happen is called the “Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) for AI Training.” As described by Professor Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, DEPA means “the model travels to the data, rather than the data travelling to the model.” The scheme envisions “Training Data Providers” (TDPs) – examples of which include hospitals, banks, and government agencies – sharing anonymized and encrypted data with a “Data Exchange Platform” (DEP). Entities called “Training Data Consumers” (TDCs) access the data stored at the DEPs to train their models. DEPs will operate what MeitY calls “hardware-based Secure Data Environments” in which “data remains encrypted and isolated even during processing.” They also enforce rules set by TDPs that describe how TDCs can use data. MeitY’s DEPA framework [PDF] says this scheme means “Differential privacy techniques are systematically applied to prevent the model from learning or revealing individual specific information,” adding “All activities inside the secure data environments are immutably logged for audit purposes, ensuring that the process is both secure and transparent.” India’s government already operates several data exchanges, but it is unclear how much work remains to make DEPA a reality. Once DEPA is working, MeitY envisions model-makers will use it to do things like “unlock currently fragmented health data to power breakthroughs in AI-driven diagnostics, drug discovery, and public health management.” The optimism extends to financial services. India is home to literally thousands of banks, and MeitY thinks “DEPA can enable secure sharing of diverse financial data, potentially extending formal credit to 400 million underserved individuals and MSMEs and fueling next-generation fintech innovation.” India’s government has long believed that if financial services companies can lend to more people, it will boost economic development. “Similarly, in Education, DEPA can overcome data interoperability challenges to enable AI-powered personalized learning for millions and create portable skill credentials essential for a future-ready workforce of its 250 million students in a $29 billion EdTech sector,” the framework states. “The successful adoption of DEPA Training across these domains is the essential catalyst for realizing India’s vision of inclusive growth and responsible AI leadership on the global stage.” While t
