item.title: BellaNaija’s Omotunde is Off to South Korea For LG Electronics Press Tour
item.description: Hey BNers! Guess who’s off to South Korea? Yours truly! I’m super excited to share that LG has invited us on a press tour to South Korea, and I honestly can’t wait to see what they have in store for us. From getting an inside look at some of LG’s innovations to visiting its facilities and flagship spaces, this promises to be an exciting opportunity to see a different side of the brand and experience some of the technology that goes into the products we use every day. Our itinerary will take us from Seoul to Busan, and while I’m looking forward to the LG experience, I’m also secretly hoping there’ll be enough time to explore a little beyond the official schedule. Because, let’s be honest, how does one travel all the way to South Korea and not try to soak in some of its beauty? And BNers, we need to talk about the K-drama dreams! If you know me, you know I’m already imagining the beautiful streets, cute cafés, familiar-looking locations, and all those little moments that make you feel like you’ve stepped right into an episode of your favourite Korean drama. Hopefully, I get a little time to wander around, discover some hidden gems, sample Korean food, and take in the culture. Who knows? I just might get to live out my K-drama princess dreams for a day or two. And before anyone asks, yes, I am fully prepared to be a little dramatic about it. If I find myself walking down a beautiful Seoul street with the perfect autumn backdrop, please allow me my main-character moment. If there’s a cute café that looks like it belongs in a romance drama, just know that I’m probably stopping for pictures. And if I happen to run into your favourite oppa while I’m out and about? Well, BNers, you’ll be the first to know! But beyond the K-drama fantasies, I’m genuinely looking forward to experiencing South Korea for myself, seeing its culture up close, discovering new places, and sharing the experience with you all. So, here’s where you come in! If you could send me anywhere in South Korea, where would it be? Is there a K-drama filming location you’ve always wanted to see? A Korean dish you think I absolutely must try? A café, shopping district, street, or attraction that deserves a spot on my itinerary? So, stay glued to BellaNaija because we’re taking this trip together. And who knows? You might just get to experience a little bit of South Korea through my eyes. Seoul, Busan, K-drama dreams, and LG adventures? I’m ready! Catch all the deets on the @bellanaija Instagram soon. Annyeonghaseyo, BNers! See you on the other side. item.title: Veekee James’ Sheer Beaded Bodice Leads Wine-Red Fashion at Zlatan Ibile’s Wedding | See Photos
item.description: Veekee James showcasing her custom wine-red corset dress and gold woven box clutch. Veekee James at a party? Trust her to come dressed like the celebration has its own red carpet. And when it’s a Nigerian wedding, with good music, beautiful traditional outfits and guests who take their fashion very seriously, you already know she’s going to have some fun with her look. Yesterday, Afrobeats star Zlatan Ibile , whose real name is Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael , and his partner, Davita Omoniyi , celebrated their traditional wedding with family, friends and some familiar faces from the entertainment industry. Among the guests was Nigerian fashion designer Veekee James, who arrived in a gorgeous wine-red and champagne creation from her own fashion label. And between the sculpted corset, the beaded sleeves and that towering gele, there was so much to admire. Veekee James in a custom wine-red sheer corset dress with metallic sequin detailing and a structured metallic gele. Let’s start with the dress. Veekee chose a floor-length, figure-hugging design featuring a sheer corset-style bodice covered in vertical rows of wine-red crystals. The sweetheart-inspired neckline extended into a high, embellished collar, while the long sheer sleeves featured rows of burgundy beads. The fitted skirt followed a mermaid silhouette, with sweeping patterns of gold sequins, wine-red embroidery and dusty-rose detailing running down to a subtle train. Structural details of the sheer corset bodice, crystal neckband, and sequin wave skirt on Veekee James’ wedding guest dress. And that gele! Veekee went for a tall, fan-pleated design in metallic champagne, giving her look even more height and making the headwrap a fashion moment of its own. She paired it with burgundy drop earrings, a structured gold woven box clutch and soft, neutral makeup that complemented the colours of her outfit. Styling details of Veekee James’ high-neck crystal collar, sheer corset bodice, and pleated metallic gele. Of course, Veekee knows her way around a corset. As the founder and creative director of her eponymous fashion label, she’s known for sculpted silhouettes, detailed beadwork and glamorous occasionwear. For Zlatan and Davita’s wedding, she brought those design elements into her own wardrobe, pairing a fitted, heavily embellished dress with a traditional gele. What we particularly love is how the colours work together. The deep wine-red gives the dress its richness, while the champagne and gold details brighten the overall look. Even with the crystals, beading and high neckline, the accessories have their place, from the matching earrings to the gold clutch. Veekee James posing alongside her husband Femi Atere at Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi’s wedding. And if you’ve been looking for wedding guest inspiration, Veekee’s outfit offers a lovely styling idea: when your dress has this much detail around the neckline, you can leave out the necklace and let your earrings and gele do their thing. item.title: Zlatan Ibile & Davita Omoniyi Celebrate Yoruba Heritage in Lemon Yellow and Mint Green
item.description: Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi celebrating their Yoruba cultural heritage during their wedding ceremony. Lemon yellow and mint green? Now that’s a colour combination we can get behind. For their second traditional wedding look, Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi ( Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael ) have switched things up, trading their earlier burgundy and ivory outfits for a softer palette that feels right at home at a Yoruba wedding. And if you thought one outfit change was enough for this celebration, you know Nigerian weddings better than that! Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi in custom Mazelle Bridal pastel Yoruba traditional attire, styled by Goodnews Emmanuel Icon. After honouring Davita’s Edo heritage in their first look, the couple are now celebrating Zlatan’s Yoruba roots in coordinated outfits by Mazelle Bridal. Davita wears a custom lemon-yellow gown with a sculpted, corset-style bodice, a sweetheart-inspired neckline and long sleeves with flared cuffs. Mint-green appliqué forms swirling, floral-inspired patterns across the bodice and fitted, floor-length skirt, with gold-toned accents adding extra detail. Davita Omoniyi showcasing her custom Mazelle Bridal outfit for her Yoruba traditional wedding look. She completes the look with a large, pleated lemon-yellow gele and matching sheer fabric draped over her arm. A green statement necklace, matching earrings and a mint-green clutch bring the accessories together, while the soft yellow and green palette gives her bridal look a fresh, coordinated finish. Davita Omoniyi wearing a pleated circular gele and sheer veil for her second traditional wedding outfit change. item.title: How AI Can Expand Opportunities for African Youth – Discussions to Expect at Goalkeepers 2026 Dakar
item.description: AI could be a great equaliser, but only if it’s built intentionally to benefit the people who need it most. Credit: Gates Foundation . During the 2026 ADF-YGL Convening in Lagos , young leaders from across the world, including Africa, gathered at Learn2Earn Academy, an AI talent factory founded by Iyinoluwa Aboyeji . There, the global leaders were introduced to a few students who have been using AI to build solutions for some of the day-to-day challenges that Africans, Nigerians specifically, face. One of them was Anas Masama, who showcased ‘Morrow’, a fintech app that allows offline transfers without internet connectivity. Anas explained that despite the wide coverage of internet providers in Nigeria, the internet’s strength fluctuates or sometimes goes offline and leaves Nigerians stranded at a point of payment. With AI, he built ‘Morrow’ to solve two problems: 1) The embarrassment that a Nigerian might feel due to bad internet connectivity. 2) Time. Anas’ invention is an example of the potential opportunities that exist when Africans leverage AI to solve basic issues. While there are concerns about the risks of AI use in Africa, including hallucinations, stereotypical results and many others, it remains one of the fastest-growing technological advancements in recent times. AI continues to grow and become more efficient, and the most urgent task Africans can embark on is to upskill in how to adopt AI for better use, so the continent doesn’t get left behind. In the 2026 Goalkeepers Report , Bill Gates calls for three actions now that will help AI improve lives and livelihoods for more people in the years ahead: Make AI tools work in every language people speak; ground AI tools in local data; and invest in people and access in the places and populations they are intended to serve. All three suggestions apply to Africa so it can properly leverage AI to expand opportunities. At present, despite how expansive AI has become, it is built in places far away from Africa. This is why Africans, who have access to local data and speak African languages, should build AI tools that incorporate local data and African languages for better use. This way, AI has access to specific data of Africans and will allow it to better understand cultural contexts and pragmatics. This will make a great equaliser rather than make things less equal. Of course, Africans still encounter basic challenges like electricity, connectivity, access to phones, and other issues, but those who have access must maximise it greatly to help others. This year’s Goalkeepers 2026 is centred around this conversation. After hosting engaging and immersive events in the Nordics and New York, Goalkeepers is coming to Dakar on October 29. This event, “Equitable AI and the Future of African Youth”, aims to discuss how AI can create opportunities for Africans across various sectors while also addressing the challenges the continent faces. item.title: Davido, Zlatan & Shoday Turn Their “Nakupenda” Performance Into a London Sing-Along
item.description: Shoday, Zlatan Ibile, and Davido performing Nakupenda live on stage during their London concert setup. Photo Credit: Davido/Instagram “Oh my God, what is this? (What is what?)” You already know what comes next. We’re taking you straight to London, where Davido , Zlatan and Shoday had an entire arena singing along to “ Nakupenda ”. And judging by the crowd, nobody needed convincing to join in. Phones were up, voices were loud, and thousands of fans were enjoying every moment of the performance. There’s something so lovely about watching a song travel from our speakers to a stage thousands of miles away, with a crowd singing every word right back to the artistes. That’s exactly what happened when Davido and Zlatan performed “Nakupenda” alongside Shoday, giving the London audience a performance filled with music, dancing and some very happy fans. Davido took to the stage in a white tank top and green trousers, moving across the platform as the audience sang along. Zlatan joined him in a tactical vest and red trousers, bringing his familiar dance moves into the mix. With dancers adding to the performance and the crowd responding to every verse, there was hardly a moment when the arena wasn’t buzzing. And can we talk about those phone flashlights? Seeing thousands of them raised across the arena while everyone sang together was such a beautiful sight. It’s one thing to enjoy “Nakupenda” through your headphones, but hearing an entire crowd sing it back to Davido, Zlatan and Shoday is a whole different experience. item.title: Milan Meets Lagos: Salone del Mobile Makes a Stunning Debut at Design Week Lagos 2026!
item.description: The global design world just got a major dose of Lagos energy! In a historic moment for the African creative scene, the world-renowned Salone del Mobile . Milano officially touched down in Nigeria for the very first time during Design Week Lagos 2026. Held at the iconic National Theatre, the high-profile gathering brought together international design heavyweights, top Nigerian architects, interior designers, business leaders, and cultural icons for an unforgettable exchange of ideas and inspiration. Leading the Italian delegation were Marco Sabetta , General Manager, Salone del Mobile and the legendary Marva Griffin Wilshire, Founder & Curator, SaloneSatellite. The strategic visit highlights Nigeria’s booming demand for luxury design and luxury living, with demand for Italian craftsmanship reaching record highs across the continent. Honors & Cultural Magic A major highlight of the week was the inaugural IDEA Honours, where Marva Griffin Wilshire received the Architectural Legacy Honour—complete with a breathtaking custom award plaque crafted by iconic Nigerian master Demas Nwoko , MFR. Also celebrated were visionary architect Lesley Lokko and celebrated artist Yinka Shonibare CBE. “Being here in Lagos today allowed us to discover remarkable new African talent and build the conditions that will help young designers forge their paths globally, ” shared an inspired Marva Griffin Wilshire. Making a New Africa From guided exhibition tours to rich panel sessions focused on this year’s theme, Making a New Africa: From Material to Market, the atmosphere was charged with ambition and creativity. Design Week Lagos founder Titi Ogufer e emphasized that Africa’s rich materials, heritage, and creative talent are ready to drive global industrial growth. With Design Week Lagos running through October 25th, the city has firmly cemented its status as Africa’s ultimate capital for design, innovation, and style. Next stop? item.title: A Royal Love Story! Zlatan Ibile & Davita Omoniyi’s Edo Traditional Wedding Looks
item.description: Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi holding hands during their Edo traditional wedding, styled by Goodnews Emmanuel Icon. What a beautiful day for love! Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi are celebrating their traditional wedding today, and we’re starting the day with their beautiful first look. The Afrobeats star and his bride-to-be have chosen to honour Davita’s Edo heritage with coordinated traditional wedding attire, from her richly embellished burgundy gown to his regal ivory outfit. And there’s so much to love about the details. For their first appearance, Zlatan, whose real name is Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael , and Davita chose to honour her Edo heritage. And what better way to celebrate love than by showing up in outfits that tell a beautiful story about where you come from? Zlatan Ibile kissing Davita Omoniyi’s hand in their custom Edo cultural attire, styled by Goodnews Emmanuel Icon. Davita looked every inch the Edo bride in a custom burgundy gown by Dova Bridals. The corseted mermaid design featured a curved sweetheart neckline, sheer long sleeves and a sweeping side train. Red crystal beads formed beautiful lattice patterns across the gown, while her traditional Okuku braided crown and layers of coral necklaces completed the look. She also carried a black horsehair fly whisk, with a sheer crimson veil draped over her crown. Davita Omoniyi as an Edo bride seated on a carved throne in a custom Dova Bridals gown. And Zlatan? The groom was every bit as regal beside his bride. He wore a custom cream robe by Deji & Kola, topped with a textured ivory coat featuring hand-stitched red beadwork along the shoulders and hem. The red details tied his outfit beautifully to Davita’s, while layers of coral beads, an ivory ceremonial cap and a carved wooden staff completed his traditional look. Zlatan Ibile wearing a custom Deji & Kola cream robe and layered coral beads for his traditional wedding. Styled by Goodnews Emmanuel Icon, the couple posed against a warm ombré backdrop, with Zlatan seated on a carved gold throne beneath a tasseled umbrella. Between the coordinated outfits, the traditional accessories and the beautiful celebration of Davita’s Edo roots, their first wedding look is one we’ll be admiring for a while. Zlatan Ibile seated on a ceremonial throne beside Davita Omoniyi for their traditional wedding feature. item.description: AI is increasingly getting good at doing some tasks, but it can never replace human workers’ judgment Autonomous cars, which may be the safest we have built, keep getting easily avoidable parking tickets. While Waymos crash far less often than human drivers over tens of millions of miles, they’re still terrible at performing basic tasks – keeping out of disabled parking spots and tow-away zones, or steering clear of a church garage during Sunday service, according to the Wall Street Journal . That is the state of AI today: impressively capable at something complex, yet embarrassingly clumsy at something easy. item.title: Wikipedia often gets taken for granted – but its history is fascinating, and its future is fragile
item.description: Wikipedia’s 68m articles have been consulted trillions of times. Not bad for a website that has barely changed since it was founded 20 years ago A few years ago, I was struck by the tension between how Wikipedia was used, and how it was talked about. Everyone was on it all the time, and yet its reputation had stalled at “don’t trust it”, because it was the “free encyclopedia that anyone can edit”. Clearly people were trusting it, so much so it had become part of the fabric of everyday life since it was founded by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger in 2001. But despite the fact it now has been consulted trillions of times by billions of people (English Wikipedia alone is 5.2bn words long), it inspires an odd lack of curiosity. Even people donating to Wikipedia might say the money was “for the factcheckers”, though there aren’t any – not paid ones, anyway. Meanwhile, the internet in the social media era had begun to feel like a much uglier place, and some digital nostalgia was setting in: here was this holdover that had somehow survived; a website that functions – and even looks – much the same as it did 20 years ago. Continue reading...

New Orleans is home to NASA’s Michoud Assembly Facility, where stages for NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and structures for Orion spacecraft are produced for the Artemis missions.

item.title: Artemis III RS-25 Engine Processing: #3 Lift
item.description: Technicians prepare to transfer the #2 RS-25 SLS (Space Launch System) rocket engine (front) to the work stand with the #3 engine (back) for integration with the Artemis III core stage rocket on Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026, inside the Vehicle Assembly Building at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. During Artemis III, the four RS‑25 engines will launch the Orion spacecraft and its crew of four into low Earth orbit, generating more than two million pounds of thrust at liftoff.

item.title: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Launches
item.description: A SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket with NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Telescope on board is seen transiting the sun during launch from Launch Complex 39A, Sunday, Aug. 30, 2026, at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

item.title: NASA's Artemis II Crew Receives Congressional Space Medal of Honor
item.description: President Donald J. Trump awarded NASA astronauts Victor Glover and Christina Koch, CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Jeremy Hansen, and NASA astronaut Reid Wiseman with the Congressional Space Medal of Honor on Aug. 28, 2026, at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.

item.title: Astronauts Anil Menon and Sophie Adenot on Spacewalk
item.description: From left, Expedition 75 flight engineers Anil Menon of NASA (partially obscured and wearing the spacesuit with a red stripe on the legs) and Sophie Adenot of ESA (European Space Agency) work together during a six‑hour and 23‑minute spacewalk outside the International Space Station.

item.title: NASA's B777 Gets New Coat of Paint
item.description: NASA's Boeing 777 returns to the agency's Langley Research Center after receiving a new paint scheme.

item.title: Colorful Collage of Tarantula Nebula
item.description: Like a collage made of layered sheets of colored cellophane, a vibrant new image layers observations of a famous star-forming nebula from NASA space telescopes. The resulting cosmic “craft” reveals new details about the star formation region known as 30 Doradus, or the Tarantula Nebula.

item.title: Perseids Meteor Shower
item.description: The constellation Orion is framed by two Perseid meteors on Aug. 12, 2018, in Cedar Breaks National Monument, Utah.

item.title: 2026 Total Solar Eclipse in Spain
item.description: A total solar eclipse is seen from San Millán de los Caballeros, Spain, Wednesday, Aug. 12, 2026.

item.title: Taking Flight to Prepare for Space
item.description: NASA astronaut candidate Adam Fuhrmann prepares for a training flight aboard NASA’s WB-57 aircraft.
